records.paid_demand: The source describes a dated regulatory requirement but says product-specific willingness to pay was not found. It reports that Companies House expects about 2.2m accounts a year, with about 75% already filed electronically; the source says most remaining filers are directors filing their own accounts, not accountants.

competitors.note: Practice-focused trial balance to accounts, iXBRL, and filing product; launch date inferred and exact date unverified.

competitors.price: £164/yr for 12 clients, £368 for 50, £744 for 150, £1,050 for 1,000 (ex VAT)

rounds.plain: The initial kill-check found no kill rule for the multi-client accountant niche at a plausible price floor, while the April 2028 commercial-software filing requirement remained in official guidance.

Validation killed the lead. K2 means at least two competing launches in six months; the source identifies AccountsGear and Taxley, though their launch timing is inferred or unverified. K4 means at least five incumbents at or below the price floor; the source lists several low-cost products. K9 is not defined in the supplied code key; the source also says statutory filing support and liability make a handover within five hours per week doubtful.

risks: The small and micro company P&L filing requirement was paused, reducing the extra disclosure work.
The market is crowded with low-cost products offering multi-client dashboards or batch filing.
Statutory filing errors and rejections may require human support; fit within ≤5 h/week is doubtful.
Product-specific willingness to pay is unverified.
records.moat: No UK or niche wedge is evident; the proposed readiness or exception queue overlaps existing batch filing and multi-client dashboards.
records.next_steps: The source says not to proceed with this lead. If revisited, it suggests a different lead: a portfolio-wide 2028-readiness audit using free Companies House bulk accounts data, with its own kill-check.
